explanations.answer: So they won't grieve like those without hope
explanations.explanation: That's the reason Paul gives: “…so that you will not grieve like the rest, who are without hope.” Notice he never says don't grieve at all. He says don't grieve like people who have no hope. I think he knows it hurts, and he's handing them something solid to hold while it does.

explanations.answer: So they can honor their memory every year
explanations.explanation: Remembering people is a lovely thing, baker, but Paul doesn't put anything on a yearly schedule here. His reason is “…so that you will not grieve like the rest, who are without hope.” The whole point is hope. Nobody's getting a calendar reminder out of this verse.

explanations.answer: So they know where each one is buried
explanations.explanation: Paul doesn't say a word about graves or where anyone is laid. He wants them informed “…so that you will not grieve like the rest, who are without hope.” That's a hope question, not a map question. Nobody is handing out directions here, friend.

Yes! Paul says “…God will bring with Jesus those who have fallen asleep in Him.” Look at how he builds it. Jesus died and rose again, so those who are in Him are not left behind. If Jesus got back up, they come along with Him.

explanations.answer: Keep them resting in the earth
explanations.explanation: That's not what Paul says, baker. He says God will bring them with Jesus. Paul uses the word asleep for those who have died in Him, and that sleep is not where the story ends. They're not stuck in the ground forever.

Remembering is sweet, but Paul promises something bigger than a memory. He says “…God will bring with Jesus those who have fallen asleep in Him.” That's an action, not just a thought. I'd say that's a lot more than a framed photo on the shelf.

Paul says the opposite, friend. He says the living “…will by no means precede those who have fallen asleep.” Nobody on earth gets a head start. In the very next verse, the dead in Christ are the first to rise.

That's right, baker. Paul says those who are alive and remain “…will by no means precede those who have fallen asleep.” The believers who have died are not at the back of the line. Nobody is cutting in front of them.

Paul doesn't list a wind here, friend. What he does list is “…with a loud command, with the voice of an archangel, and with the trumpet of God…” Three sounds, and the third one is the trumpet. Easy to mix up when they're all this big.

Water doesn't make the list in this verse, friend. Paul names “…a loud command…” “…the voice of an archangel…” and “…the trumpet of God…” So the missing piece is the trumpet. It's easy to mix up sounds when they're all this big.

Yes, baker. Paul says “…the dead in Christ will be the first to rise.” Those who died believing in Jesus go first. Paul follows it up with “Therefore encourage one another with these words.” (1 Thessalonians 4:18), so this is meant to lift people up.

The living come second, friend. Paul says “…the dead in Christ will be the first to rise.” and only then, “After that,” do those who are alive and remain get caught up. So the dead are first. The living wait their turn.

Paul doesn't mention elders at all in this verse. He says “…the dead in Christ will be the first to rise.” It's about everyone who died in Christ, not a special group with a title. Nobody needs a title to be first here.
That's right, baker. Paul says the living “…will be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air.” The word that stands out to me is together. Nobody makes the trip alone.
Paul says exactly that, friend. The living “…will be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air.” So the living and the dead in Christ meet Him together. That one is true.
Always! Paul says, “And so we will always be with the Lord.” Then he adds, “Therefore encourage one another with these words.” (1 Thessalonians 4:18) It's not a quick visit, baker.
Sometimes is not in Paul's vocabulary here, friend. He says, “And so we will always be with the Lord.” It's not on and off. It's always.
Paul doesn't say briefly. He says, “And so we will always be with the Lord.” That's no pop-in visit, baker. Always is about as far from brief as a word gets.
That's right, baker. Paul says, “Therefore encourage one another with these words.” The words are for lifting each other up. They're meant to be shared, not kept in a drawer.
Paul says the opposite, friend. He writes, “Therefore encourage one another with these words.” He wants the church to use what he just told them to lift each other up. So that statement is true.

explanations.answer: Like a thief in the night
explanations.explanation: You got it, baker. Paul says, “…the Day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night.” A thief doesn't send a schedule. That's the picture Paul wants stuck in their minds.

explanations.answer: Like a sunrise after a long night
explanations.explanation: A sunrise at least comes with a glow in the sky, friend. Paul uses a different picture: “…the Day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night.” A thief doesn't give notice. That's the picture he uses.

explanations.answer: Like a king with a long parade
explanations.explanation: A parade has banners and a long line of folks to see coming, baker. Paul's picture is the opposite. He says, “…the Day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night.” It's a thief, not a parade.

That's right, baker. Paul says “destruction will come upon them suddenly…” and he says it comes while people are saying, “Peace and security…” That word suddenly matters. It lands right in the middle of everybody saying things are fine.

Rescue is the opposite of what Paul says here, friend. While people are saying, “Peace and security…” he says “destruction will come upon them suddenly…” Then he adds that it comes “…like labor pains on a pregnant woman…” Labor pains don't send a warning text first.
No blessing in this verse, baker. Look at the contrast. People are saying, “Peace and security…” and what comes next is “…destruction…” The calm talk and the sudden arrival are a world apart.

Paul says the opposite, friend. After saying destruction will come upon them suddenly, he adds, “…they will not escape.” So the people saying, “Peace and security…” don't slip out of it. That statement is false.
That's right, baker. Paul says destruction will come upon them suddenly, “…like labor pains on a pregnant woman, and they will not escape.” There's no back door. They will not escape.

explanations.answer: They are not in the darkness

Paul never says that, friend. Praying is a good thing, baker, but it's not the reason Paul gives here. He says, “But you, brothers, are not in the darkness so that this day should overtake you like a thief.” The reason is where they stand, in the light and not the darkness. That's the whole point of the verse.

Paul says the opposite, friend. He writes, “So then, let us not sleep as the others do, but let us remain awake and sober.” They belong to the day, so they stay awake and sober. That statement is true.

Those are good words, friend, but they're not what Paul uses in this verse. He says, “…putting on the breastplate of faith and love…” That's what this breastplate is made of. The helmet comes next.

Courage and strength sound like they'd fit, baker, but Paul doesn't list them here. He says, “…putting on the breastplate of faith and love…” It's faith and love that guard the chest. Even in my apron I'd take that.

Paul says the opposite, friend. He writes, “For God has not appointed us to suffer wrath, but to obtain salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ.” So wrath is not what the believers were appointed for. Salvation is.

Yes, baker! Paul says Jesus “…died for us so that, whether we are awake or asleep, we may live together with Him.” Awake or asleep, the answer is the same. It's together with Him.

Paul says almost the opposite, friend. He says Jesus “…died for us so that, whether we are awake or asleep, we may live together with Him.” The word is together, not apart. Nobody is stuck waiting alone.

Alone doesn't fit Paul's words, baker. He says Jesus “…died for us so that, whether we are awake or asleep, we may live together with Him.” The word is together, and it's together with Him. That's the whole comfort of it.
That's right, baker. Paul says, “Therefore encourage and build one another up, just as you are already doing.” Notice the last part. He's not scolding them, because they're already doing it.

Praying for each other is good, friend, but it's not what Paul adds in this verse. He says, “Therefore encourage and build one another up, just as you are already doing.” The new thing is building one another up. And he says they're already doing it.

That's a kind thing to do, baker, but Paul doesn't say it in this verse. He writes, “Therefore encourage and build one another up, just as you are already doing.” Encouraging and building up go together, one lifting the other. And he says they're already at it, so that's a pat on the back before it's a to-do list.
